_comment: 2D RosettaStone — reverse-engineered from HITOS IfcAnnotation (9203 entities merged into HITOS_extracted.db) + AIA/NCS drafting conventions. Same pattern as 3D RosettaStone: we don't know the authoring tool's rules, but we infer them from the IFC output and prove them with SQL against the extracted DB.

_ifc_standard.adoptable: Yes — this is standard IFC. Every BIM authoring tool (Revit, ArchiCAD, Tekla) exports IfcAnnotation the same way. The structure is universal; only the content varies per project.

storey_distribution._insight: Grid defined once at main floor (1.etg), sparse copies on other storeys

column_alignment._insight: 1722/2920 annotations align with IfcColumn centroids within 0.3m — grid lines pass through columns

size_classes.grid_bubble_tail: H_170mm, V_460mm (median — short stubs at grid line ends)

view_definitions._rule: Each view = one cut plane + one bundle. The bundle defines which elements appear and how. A floor plan is not 'everything at Z' — it's a curated group: walls(cut) + doors(symbol) + windows(symbol) + furniture(projection). Each view type has its own bundle.

floor_plan.source_sql: SELECT DISTINCT name, elevation FROM spatial_structure WHERE type='IfcBuildingStorey'

cut._rule: Elements whose Z range intersects the cut plane → drawn SOLID with cut line weight
cut.source_sql: SELECT m.*, r.* FROM elements_meta m JOIN elements_rtree r ON m.id=r.id WHERE r.minZ <= ?cut AND r.maxZ >= ?cut AND m.ifc_class IN ('IfcWall','IfcWallStandardCase','IfcDoor','IfcWindow','IfcColumn')

projection_below._rule: Elements fully below cut plane but on same storey → drawn DASHED/DOTTED with light weight
projection_below.source_sql: SELECT m.*, r.* FROM elements_meta m JOIN elements_rtree r ON m.id=r.id WHERE r.maxZ < ?cut AND r.maxZ > ?storey_elev AND m.ifc_class IN ('IfcFurnishingElement','IfcStair','IfcRamp')

omit._rule: Elements above cut plane or floor slabs (you're standing on them) → not drawn

floor_plan.status: PARTIAL — walls/windows/doors drawn, furniture dotted shown, but bundle not formalized

cut.source_sql: SELECT m.*, r.* FROM elements_meta m JOIN elements_rtree r ON m.id=r.id WHERE r.minY <= ?cut AND r.maxY >= ?cut

projection_beyond._rule: Elements behind the cut plane, visible in depth
projection_beyond.source_sql: SELECT m.*, r.* FROM elements_meta m JOIN elements_rtree r ON m.id=r.id WHERE r.minY > ?cut AND m.ifc_class IN ('IfcWall','IfcWindow','IfcDoor')

visible.source_sql: SELECT m.*, r.* FROM elements_meta m JOIN elements_rtree r ON m.id=r.id WHERE r.minY <= ?face + 0.5

cut.source_sql: SELECT m.*, r.* FROM elements_meta m JOIN elements_rtree r ON m.id=r.id WHERE m.ifc_class IN ('IfcRoof','IfcSlab') AND m.storey=(SELECT name FROM spatial_structure WHERE type='IfcBuildingStorey' ORDER BY CAST(elevation AS REAL) DESC LIMIT 1)

grid_lines._rule: A grid line marks any alignment axis — where multiple elements share a coordinate. HITOS: columns. SampleHouse: wall faces and window rows. The general rule: cluster element face positions, rank by shared count, top N become grid axes.

_evidence.hitos: 1722/2920 annotations align with IfcColumn centroids within 0.3m

sh_x_axes.X=0.00: 12 walls share minX — building left edge
sh_x_axes.X=0.42: 5+4 walls share face — interior wall line
sh_x_axes.X=8.38: 4+8 walls share face — interior wall line
sh_x_axes.X=8.80: 9 walls share maxX — building right edge
sh_x_axes.X=0.21: 6 windows share X — window row alignment
sh_x_axes.X=8.59: 4 windows share X — window row alignment

sh_y_axes.Y=0.00: 6 walls share maxY — building front edge
sh_y_axes.Y=-0.42: 4+8 walls share face — front wall inner line
sh_y_axes.Y=-17.38: 5+4 walls share face — rear wall inner line
sh_y_axes.Y=-17.80: 9 walls share minY — building rear edge

detect_grid._algorithm: Universal alignment detection — works for any building, with or without columns

step_1_collect_faces.source_sql: SELECT ROUND(r.minX,2) as face FROM elements_meta m JOIN elements_rtree r ON m.id=r.id WHERE m.ifc_class NOT IN ('IfcAnnotation','IfcOpeningElement') UNION ALL SELECT ROUND(r.maxX,2) FROM elements_meta m JOIN elements_rtree r ON m.id=r.id WHERE m.ifc_class NOT IN ('IfcAnnotation','IfcOpeningElement')
step_1_collect_faces.description: Collect all element face positions (minX, maxX, minY, maxY) into candidate pools

step_2_cluster.method: GROUP BY ROUND(face, 2), COUNT(*) as shared_count
step_2_cluster.description: Group faces within 20mm tolerance, rank by how many elements share that position

step_3_filter.description: An axis needs >= 3 elements aligned to qualify as a grid line. Filters noise from single-element coincidences.

step_4_rank.description: Columns trump walls trump openings. Within each tier, higher shared count = stronger axis.

step_5_label.vertical_axes: A, B, C, D... (left to right by ascending X)

grid_bubbles._rule: Circle at each grid line terminus. Label: A,B,C... for vertical lines (left to right), 1,2,3... for horizontal lines (bottom to top). HITOS evidence: bubble tails are 170-460mm stubs.
grid_bubbles.placement: end of grid line, beyond extension

dimension_chains._rule: Three tiers outside the building outline. Reading direction: L→R (horizontal) or bottom→top (vertical). Tick marks (oblique strokes), not arrows. All values in mm, no unit suffix.
dimension_chains._evidence: HITOS has zero IfcTextLiteral — dimensions are view-generated, not stored in IFC. This confirms dimensions are derived from geometry, not authored separately.

tier_1_overall._rule: Outermost string: total building extent per axis
tier_1_overall.source_sql: SELECT MIN(r.minX), MAX(r.maxX), MIN(r.minY), MAX(r.maxY) FROM elements_rtree r JOIN elements_meta m ON m.id=r.id WHERE m.ifc_class NOT IN ('IfcAnnotation')

tier_2_bay._rule: Middle string: grid-to-grid distances (structural bay spacing)
tier_2_bay.source: consecutive differences between grid_lines.x_positions or grid_lines.y_positions

tier_3_opening._rule: Innermost string: wall-to-opening and opening widths along each wall run
tier_3_opening.source_sql: SELECT m.ifc_class, m.element_name, r.minX, r.maxX FROM elements_meta m JOIN elements_rtree r ON m.id=r.id WHERE m.ifc_class IN ('IfcDoor','IfcWindow') AND m.storey=? ORDER BY r.minX

label_template._rule: All labels, tags, symbols, dimensions, and styles come from 2D_metadata.db — a complete template system extracted from TB-LKTN RUMAH RAKYAT. Any project plugs into this template; only the geometry changes.

tables.2d_room_label: Bilingual room names: BILIK/BEDROOM, DAPUR/KITCHEN + codes (BLK, BM, RT)
tables.2d_annotation_tag: Element tags: D1/D2 doors, W1/W2 windows, hexagon/diamond shapes
tables.2d_dimension_style: Tick marks 45°, 3 tier offsets (10/18/26mm), mm units, no decimals
tables.2d_grid_style: ALPHA horizontal, NUMERIC vertical, bubble radius 4mm, dash-dot
tables.2d_drawing_style: Line weight/color/fill per ifc_class per view type (19 entries)
tables.2d_drawing_symbol: Kitchen sink, basin, WC, shower, electrical — with sizes
tables.2d_drawing_type: 8 view types: floor, elect, roof, 4 elevations, reflected ceiling
tables.2d_heading_style: Font size/weight/alignment per label type (10 styles)
tables.2d_finish_type: Material callouts: CT, CR, V1-V5, G1, R1-R2
tables.2d_level_marker: GRD LEVEL, 1ST FLOOR, ROOF LEVEL with elevations
tables.2d_sheet_template: A1/A3 paper sizes with margins and title block width

label_template.status: DONE — 14 tables, fully seeded from TB-LKTN

completeness._note: SVG writer (drawing_writer.py) already implements most patterns. DXF writer (drawing_writer_dxf.py) covers floor plan + elevation only. The rosetta_2d.json documents the proven patterns, not redesigns them.

DONE_in_SVG.view_definitions.roof_plan: draw_roof_plan() — ridge, slope arrows, eave labels
DONE_in_SVG.grid_lines.detect: derive_grids() — wall centroid clustering, merge tolerance 500mm
DONE_in_SVG.grid_lines.grid_bubbles: circles with A,B,C / 1,2,3 labels both ends

DONE_in_DXF.grid_lines: via SVG (not yet ported to DXF)
DONE_in_DXF.guid_xdata: BIMGUID xdata on each polyline (Task 1 of 2D_007)

GAP_DXF_port: grid_lines + bubbles (SVG done, DXF not yet)
GAP_new_features: element_tags (door D01/window W01 labels — not in SVG)
completeness.next_priority: Code alignment detection algorithm (cluster element faces, rank by shared count) → then port SVG grid/dimension/label to DXF
